resources.string: Ten minutes or more, comfortably warm, about 1–2 hours before bed.
Warming up helps your body shed heat afterwards, and that drop in core temperature comes with sleepiness.
Put the phone and laptop away and switch to something on paper, or nothing at all.
Bright screens late in the evening hold back melatonin and can push your body clock later.
Lab studies and a 2022 expert consensus.
Spend five minutes writing what you need to do tomorrow. Be specific.
Parking tomorrow\'s tasks on paper can quiet the mind. In one study, people who wrote specific lists fell asleep sooner.
Breathe in for about 4 seconds and out for about 6: around six breaths a minute.
Slow breathing with a longer out-breath can help you feel calmer. People report better sleep after a few weeks of practice.
Small studies and a 2026 review; mostly self-reported.
Move your attention slowly from your feet to your head, noticing without changing anything.
Mindfulness practice improved sleep quality in several trials, mostly in how rested people felt.
Tense one muscle group for about 5 seconds, then let it go for 15, from hands to feet.
Letting go of tension can help you settle. Treat it as something pleasant, not a task.
Listed as an option in 2021 sleep-medicine guidelines.
A book or magazine under a warm, low lamp.
A quiet, screen-free activity in dim light makes winding down easier.
Indirect: studies on evening light and screens.
Slow, easy stretches for about ten minutes. Nothing strenuous.
Gentle movement can ease the day\'s tension. Direct sleep studies are few.
A few lines about the day, or three good things.
Writing things down may ease bedtime worry. The evidence is early.
Air the room, dim the lights and choose bedding that won\'t make you too warm.
A hot room makes sleep lighter and more broken.
Reviews of bedroom temperature and sleep.
Low, steady noise with a timer, if your room is noisy.
Steady noise can mask sudden sounds. Earplugs often work better, and the evidence for noise is very limited.
A 2021 review rated it very low; a 2026 lab study found pink noise cut REM sleep.
Bright screens late in the evening can delay your body clock.
Studies on evening light and screens.
Games and bright screens can keep your mind and body clock up.
Studies on evening light and screens.
Even and bright, like a fan
Deep and low, like distant surf
Hush masks background noise. Keep it low; for sudden noises, earplugs work better.
Your media volume is high. Turn it down for Hush.
Anything calm you enjoy before bed.
